page: Amazon Web Services c6g.medium is a compute-optimized instance powered by a custom AWS Graviton processor using the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. This server features 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU running at 2.5 GHz, with no hyperthreading. It is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Cache specifications include 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local NVMe storage, has no GPU accelerators, and operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the c6g.medium delivers average single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1493.38. However, due to its single-core limitation, multi-core performance is constrained, matching the single-core score of 1493.38 and placing it in the lower performance tier. Memory bandwidth is also limited, measuring 59.29 GB/sec for cached small blocks and dropping to 19.65 GB/sec for read-only large blocks. Other benchmarks, such as Geekbench single-core (934.0) and multi-core (933.0), reflect its entry-level compute profile. Cryptographic performance is supported by hardware AES acceleration, though other extended instruction sets are absent.

Given its hardware profile, the c6g.medium is designed for lightweight, single-threaded workloads that benefit from dedicated ARM64 CPU resources without requiring high memory capacity or local storage. It is suitable for basic web serving, small-scale Redis operations, and simple utility scripting. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a low-cost entry point into the AWS Graviton ecosystem, allowing developers to test and run ARM-native applications with dedicated CPU allocation at a minimal resource footprint.
